knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Products

question.:question/problem:
Express the following as a constant multiple of a single trigonometric ratio.

$$
2\sin\left(17^\circ\right)\cos\left(17^\circ\right)
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=17^\circ$. Recall $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
2\sin x\cos x &=\left[2\sin x\cos x\right] \\ &=\sin(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute $x=17^\circ$ and double the whole angle: $2x=34^\circ$. The result is

$$
\sin\left(34^\circ\right) .
$$

knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Products

question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=17^\circ$. Expand the square and combine the squared terms.

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\sin x+\cos x)^2 &=\sin^2 x+2\sin x\cos x+\cos^2 x \\ &=1+2\sin x\cos x \\ &=1+\sin(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\sin^2 x+\cos^2 x=1$ and $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

Substitute $x=17^\circ$ and double the whole angle: $2x=34^\circ$. The result is

$$
1+\sin\left(34^\circ\right) .
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=17^\circ$. Expand the square and combine the squared terms.

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\sin x-\cos x)^2 &=\sin^2 x-2\sin x\cos x+\cos^2 x \\ &=1-2\sin x\cos x \\ &=1-\sin(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\sin^2 x+\cos^2 x=1$ and $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

Substitute $x=17^\circ$ and double the whole angle: $2x=34^\circ$. The result is

$$
1-\sin\left(34^\circ\right) .
$$
